"Amshaj": that is, mixtures of the woman's fluid and the man's fluid.

"Nabtalihi": that is, We test him with the obligations, with the command and the prohibition, when he becomes fit for that through puberty and reason.

"Inna hadaynahu al-sabil": that is, We made clear to him the path of guidance through the sending of messengers and the sending down of books.

"Inna aʿtadna": that is, We prepared.

"Salasil": that is, they will be dragged by them into the fire of Hell.

"Aghlalan": that is, around their necks.

"Saʿiran": that is, a fire kindled and inflamed.

"Inna al-abrar": that is, those who obey God and His Messenger, truthful in their faith, their words and their conditions.

"Mizajuha": that is, that with which it is mixed and blended.

"Yufajjirunaha": that is, they cause it to flow and gush wherever they wish.

"Sharruhu mustatiran": that is, extended, long, widespread and spreading.

"ʿAbusan": that is, the faces will be contorted from its length and severity.

"Nadratan wa surura": that is, beauty and radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts.

Explanation of the verses:

God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ He, may He be exalted, informs about Adam, father of mankind (peace be upon him), that there came upon him a period of time which may have been forty years, while he was a form of clay that sticks together, with no spirit in it. At that time he was not a thing with distinction or elevation to be mentioned. This first man, Adam, is the one of whom God informed concerning the beginning of his affair. And His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture﴾ informs that He created the human being, who is the son of Adam, from a drop (nutfah), which is what drips and trickles from the man's fluid and the woman's fluid. The meaning of amshaj is mixtures of the man's fluid and the woman's fluid; this is the origin of the creation of the human being, the son of Adam. His saying ﴿We test him﴾ means We test him with the obligations, with the command and the prohibition, and that is when he becomes fit for them through puberty and reason. For this reason He made him hearing and seeing, since with the existence of hearing and sight together, or one of them, the obligation is completed; if both are absent, there is no obligation, for lack of the capacity to fulfil it.

And His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿We guided him to the way﴾ means We made clear to him the path of guidance through the sending of messengers and the sending down of books. Through this there also became clear to him the path of error and destruction, for they are the two highways: if one recognises one of them, one recognises the other. In that respect he will either take the path of guidance and be grateful (shakur), or take the path of error and destruction and be ungrateful (kafur). The grateful one is the believer, truthful in his faith, obedient to his Lord; the ungrateful one is the one who denies the signs of God and His meeting. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾ and the verses that follow begin to explain what has been prepared for each of those who follow the path of rectitude and those who follow the path of error. He begins with what has been prepared for those who follow the path of error, briefly stating the punishment prepared for them, in contrast to what has been prepared for those who follow the path of rectitude, for that is a bliss whose details are beloved and whose elaboration in description is desired. So He says: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles﴾, by which they will be dragged in the Fire; and shackles by which their hands will be bound to their necks; and a blazing fire and a flaming Hellfire.

This is a summary of what has been prepared for those who follow the path of error. As for those who follow the path of rectitude, He has explained it in His saying ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾, that is, the believers who obey, in sincerity toward God and the Messenger, ﴿will drink from a cup﴾ full of drink whose mixture is camphor, mixed with camphor for its coolness, the whiteness of its colour and the pleasantness of its fragrance; a spring from which the servants of God drink, for the sweetness and clarity of its water. It becomes as if it were a vessel from which they drink; therefore He said "they drink from it" [bi-ha] and did not say "from which they drink" [minha]. And His saying ﴿they cause it to gush forth in abundance﴾ means they make it flow and gush wherever they wish, within their chambers, their palaces and their gatherings of felicity. His saying ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾ breaks the account of their bliss to mention some of their virtues, as encouragement to their deeds and their bliss, and then He returns to presenting the bliss, saying ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾: that is, in the abode of the world they used to fulfil their vows, which are the acts of obedience they bind themselves to for their Lord, such as prayer, fasting, pilgrimage and charity, seeking nearness to their Lord and approach to Him, so that they may secure His pleasure, and that is the ultimate aim of their hopes. And His saying "and they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread" means that in their lives they feared the Day of Reckoning, the Day of Punishment, a day whose evil was pervasive and spreading. Along with that, ﴿they give food, despite their love for it﴾, that is, despite their love of it, their desire for it and their eagerness for it, they give it to ﴿the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾: the needy, poor, whose dwelling is poverty and whom need has humbled; the orphan who has no guardian and no wealth; and the captive, imprisoned, far from home and distant from visitation, who has no known origin or lineage. They feed them while the tongue of their state, or their speech, says: "We feed you only for the sake of God; we do not desire from you any reward by which you would repay us on any day, nor any thanks that would reach us from you." ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, that is, a face that is contorted, darkened, heavy, long and unbearable. God responded to them and fulfilled their hopes by His bounty: He protected them from the evil of that frowning, grievous day, bestowed upon them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them, for their patience in doing righteous deeds and in abstaining from what is forbidden, with a Garden and silk; and what will be mentioned after this in the following verses.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The explanation of the origin of the human being, the father and the son, and what this indicates of God's bounty and generosity toward His servants.

2- The faculties of hearing and sight, their existence together or the existence of one of them, are necessary for the obligation, along with the intellect.

3- The explanation that a person has two paths before him, and let him take whichever he wills; each path ends him at a goal. The path of rectitude leads to Paradise, the abode of bliss, and the path of error leads to the abode of misery, Hellfire.

4- The obligation to fulfil vows: whoever vows something to God must fulfil his vow, unless he vows an act of disobedience, in which case it is not permissible for him to fulfil that vow. 5- Encouragement to feed food to those in need of it: the poor, the orphan and the captive.

God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Has there come upon man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?﴾ He, may He be exalted, informs about Adam, father of mankind (peace be upon him), that there came upon him a period of time which may have been forty years, while he was a form of clay that sticks together, with no spirit in it. At that time he was not a thing with distinction or elevation to be mentioned. This first man, Adam, is the one of whom God informed concerning the beginning of his affair. And His saying ﴿Indeed, We created man from a sperm-drop mixture﴾ informs that He created the human being, who is the son of Adam, from a drop (nutfah), which is what drips and trickles from the man's fluid and the woman's fluid. The meaning of amshaj is mixtures of the man's fluid and the woman's fluid; this is the origin of the creation of the human being, the son of Adam. His saying ﴿We test him﴾ means We test him with the obligations, with the command and the prohibition, and that is when he becomes fit for them through puberty and reason. For this reason He made him hearing and seeing, since with the existence of hearing and sight together, or one of them, the obligation is completed; if both are absent, there is no obligation, for lack of the capacity to fulfil it.

And His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿We guided him to the way﴾ means We made clear to him the path of guidance through the sending of messengers and the sending down of books. Through this there also became clear to him the path of error and destruction, for they are the two highways: if one recognises one of them, one recognises the other. In that respect he will either take the path of guidance and be grateful (shakur), or take the path of error and destruction and be ungrateful (kafur). The grateful one is the believer, truthful in his faith, obedient to his Lord; the ungrateful one is the one who denies the signs of God and His meeting. His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾ and the verses that follow begin to explain what has been prepared for each of those who follow the path of rectitude and those who follow the path of error. He begins with what has been prepared for those who follow the path of error, briefly stating the punishment prepared for them, in contrast to what has been prepared for those who follow the path of rectitude, for that is a bliss whose details are beloved and whose elaboration in description is desired. So He says: ﴿Indeed, We have prepared for the disbelievers chains and shackles﴾, by which they will be dragged in the Fire; and shackles by which their hands will be bound to their necks; and a blazing fire and a flaming Hellfire.

This is a summary of what has been prepared for those who follow the path of error. As for those who follow the path of rectitude, He has explained it in His saying ﴿Indeed, the righteous﴾, that is, the believers who obey, in sincerity toward God and the Messenger, ﴿will drink from a cup﴾ full of drink whose mixture is camphor, mixed with camphor for its coolness, the whiteness of its colour and the pleasantness of its fragrance; a spring from which the servants of God drink, for the sweetness and clarity of its water. It becomes as if it were a vessel from which they drink; therefore He said "they drink from it" [bi-ha] and did not say "from which they drink" [minha]. And His saying ﴿they cause it to gush forth in abundance﴾ means they make it flow and gush wherever they wish, within their chambers, their palaces and their gatherings of felicity. His saying ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾ breaks the account of their bliss to mention some of their virtues, as encouragement to their deeds and their bliss, and then He returns to presenting the bliss, saying ﴿They fulfil their vows﴾: that is, in the abode of the world they used to fulfil their vows, which are the acts of obedience they bind themselves to for their Lord, such as prayer, fasting, pilgrimage and charity, seeking nearness to their Lord and approach to Him, so that they may secure His pleasure, and that is the ultimate aim of their hopes. And His saying "and they fear a Day whose evil will be widespread" means that in their lives they feared the Day of Reckoning, the Day of Punishment, a day whose evil was pervasive and spreading. Along with that, ﴿they give food, despite their love for it﴾, that is, despite their love of it, their desire for it and their eagerness for it, they give it to ﴿the needy, the orphan and the captive﴾: the needy, poor, whose dwelling is poverty and whom need has humbled; the orphan who has no guardian and no wealth; and the captive, imprisoned, far from home and distant from visitation, who has no known origin or lineage. They feed them while the tongue of their state, or their speech, says: "We feed you only for the sake of God; we do not desire from you any reward by which you would repay us on any day, nor any thanks that would reach us from you." ﴿Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day that is frowning﴾, that is, a face that is contorted, darkened, heavy, long and unbearable. God responded to them and fulfilled their hopes by His bounty: He protected them from the evil of that frowning, grievous day, bestowed upon them radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts, and rewarded them, for their patience in doing righteous deeds and in abstaining from what is forbidden, with a Garden and silk; and what will be mentioned after this in the following verses.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The explanation of the origin of the human being, the father and the son, and what this indicates of God's bounty and generosity toward His servants.

2- The faculties of hearing and sight, their existence together or the existence of one of them, are necessary for the obligation, along with the intellect.

3- The explanation that a person has two paths before him, and let him take whichever he wills; each path ends him at a goal. The path of rectitude leads to Paradise, the abode of bliss, and the path of error leads to the abode of misery, Hellfire.

4- The obligation to fulfil vows: whoever vows something to God must fulfil his vow, unless he vows an act of disobedience, in which case it is not permissible for him to fulfil that vow. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 76, verses 13–22:

Explanation of the words:

ʿAlā al-arāʾik (on the couches): i.e., on the beds within canopies. The singular of arāʾik is arīka.

Wa-lā zamharīran (nor any bitter cold): i.e., nor severe cold, nor moonlight, for it is illuminated by itself.

Wa-dāniyatan (and near): i.e., near to them are the shades of the trees of Paradise.

Wa-dhullilat quṭūfuhā tadhlīlan (and its fruit-clusters will be made easy to reach): i.e., such that the believer can reach them standing, sitting, or lying down.

Wa-akwāb (and cups): i.e., drinking vessels without handles.

Min fiḍḍa (of silver): i.e., one can see its inside from its outside.

Qaddarūhā taqdīran (they will have measured them with precise measure): i.e., measured according to the drinkers, without excess or deficiency.

Wa-yusqawna fīhā kaʾsan (and they will be given to drink a cup): i.e., of wine.

Kāna mizājuhā zanjabīlan (its mixture will be ginger): i.e., that with which it is mixed is ginger.

Mukhalladūn (everlasting): i.e., with the attributes of youths who do not grow old.

Luʾluʾan manthūran (scattered pearls): i.e., from a string or from their shells, because of their beauty and beauty of appearance and their dispersal in service.

Wa-idhā ra'ayta thamma (and when you look there): i.e., in Paradise you see bliss that cannot be described and a vast kingdom that cannot be measured.

Thiyāb sundus (garments of fine silk): i.e., silk.

Wa-istabraq (and brocade): i.e., what is thick of brocade.

Wa-ḥullū (and they will be adorned): i.e., the angels will adorn them with it.

Sharāban ṭahūran (a pure drink): i.e., surpassing the two previous kinds, and therefore its giving to drink is attributed to God, Mighty and Majestic.

Inna hādhā (indeed this): i.e., the bliss.

Mashkūran (appreciated): i.e., pleasing and accepted.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to mention what God, exalted is He, has prepared for the righteous believing servants who fear Him. He, exalted, says: ﴿Reclining⟩ in Paradise ﴿on couches⟩, which are beds within canopies, ﴿they will see therein⟩, i.e., in Paradise, ﴿neither sun nor bitter cold⟩. If "sun" means the known star, then "bitter cold" means the moon, so there is no sun in Paradise and no moon; and if "sun" means heat, then "bitter cold" means cold, and there is neither heat nor cold in Paradise. Both meanings are intended and realized: there is no sun or moon in Paradise because there is no need for them, and likewise no heat or cold.

﴿And near them its shades⟩, i.e., its trees are close to them, so they are shaded by them and find in that shade the pleasure, ease and enjoyment, even though there is no sun requiring shade. ﴿And its fruit-clusters are made completely accessible⟩, i.e., the fruit picked from its trees is made easy for them, so that the one standing, the one sitting, and the one lying down can reach it, without thorns and without distance, easy to take, because the abode is a abode of bliss, happiness, comfort, spirit and sweet basil. ﴿And there will be circulated among them vessels of silver⟩, i.e., the pure servants will circulate among them with vessels of silver and of gold, ﴿and cups⟩, i.e., drinking vessels without handles, which exist by God's grace and generosity, ﴿glass of silver⟩, whose inside can be seen from its outside because its material is silver and its clarity is the clarity of glass; this is why it is called qārūra and its plural is qawārīr. ﴿They will have measured them with precise measure⟩, i.e., the serving attendants have measured them so that they are neither excessive, overflowing, nor deficient, so that their appearance is not spoiled. And His saying ﴿and they will be given to drink therein a cup⟩, i.e., wine, ﴿whose mixture is ginger⟩, i.e., that with which it is mixed, from a spring in Paradise ﴿called Salsabīl⟩. And His saying, exalted, ﴿and there will circulate among them youths made everlasting⟩, i.e., there will circulate around those righteous ones in Paradise youths, boys, who are everlasting, who do not age and do not die, their state always that of youths, unchanging. ﴿And when you see them⟩ and look at them, ﴿you would think them⟩ in their beauty and their dispersal in service here and there, ﴿scattered pearls⟩.

God says to His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And when you look there⟩, i.e., there in Paradise, ﴿you will see bliss⟩ that cannot be described ﴿and a great kingdom⟩ whose extent cannot be measured. ﴿Upon them will be garments of green fine silk and brocade⟩: God informs that upon them, i.e., above them, are garments of fine green silk and brocade, which is what is thick of brocade. Some garments of brocade have inner linings and some have outer layers; the linings are what lies beneath the outer layers. And His saying, exalted, ﴿and they will be adorned with bracelets of silver⟩, i.e., their Lord will adorn them, while they are in the abode of His honor, with bracelets of silver and also of gold, as the opposite is omitted when the mentioned indicates it, like the Qur'anic phrase "garments that protect you from the heat," meaning and others that protect you from the cold. And His saying ﴿and their Lord will give them to drink a pure drink⟩: this differs from what was mentioned before; this is a special honor, namely that God Himself gives them to drink, and that this drink reaches a great degree of purity by its description as pure. It is said to them, as an honor to them and an incentive to others from the people of the world who hear this honoring address: indeed this bliss, of gardens, springs, couches, youths, food, drink, clothing and so on, ﴿is for you a reward⟩ for your faith and piety, ﴿and your striving has been appreciated⟩, i.e., your deeds in the world have been pleasing and accepted.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Affirmation of the doctrine of resurrection and recompense by mention of images of the otherworldly reward.

2- The prohibition of using vessels of gold and silver, based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "They are for them in this world and for us in the Hereafter."

3- The prohibition of wine, based on the hadith: "Whoever drinks wine in this world will not drink it in the Hereafter if he dies considering it permissible."

4- The legitimacy of having righteous servants who serve a person, and his showing them kindness.

5- The prohibition of men wearing silk, and its permissibility for women, and likewise gold.
